project: JARVIS TRADER Sprint 17 — The Database Fix
description: Sprint 16 US-1603 uncovered three critical database blockers that corrupt every P&L metric, validation gate, and learning loop feed in the system: (1) engine/jarvis_trader.db is a 0-byte ghost file — real DB is engine/data/jarvis_trader.db, (2) all paper trades have NULL pnl because close_trade() never writes P&L to SQLite, (3) 416 trades exist in JSON files vs only 6 in SQLite — JSON is the real source of truth but all endpoints query SQLite. These must be fixed before any MES experiment work, signal frequency verification, or learning loop feedback can be trusted. After the DB fix trilogy, Sprint 17 completes with n-autoresearch file recovery and MES experiment foundation setup.

userStories.title: Fix ghost DB path — canonicalize to engine/data/jarvis_trader.db
userStories.description: As the system operator, I need all database connections to point to the real database at engine/data/jarvis_trader.db instead of the 0-byte ghost at engine/jarvis_trader.db so that every endpoint, test, and learning loop reads real data.
acceptanceCriteria: Search all Python files in engine/ for references to 'jarvis_trader.db' that do NOT include 'data/' in the path: grep -rn "jarvis_trader.db" engine/ --include='*.py' | grep -v 'data/jarvis_trader'. List every file and line number found.

For each file found: update the path string to 'data/jarvis_trader.db' or use the canonical path constant if one exists. If a DB_PATH constant exists in engine/config.py or engine/database/, update it there and confirm all other files import from it rather than hardcoding the path.

Confirm engine/data/jarvis_trader.db exists and passes PRAGMA integrity_check: cd engine && .venv/Scripts/python -c "import sqlite3; conn = sqlite3.connect('data/jarvis_trader.db'); print(conn.execute('PRAGMA integrity_check').fetchone())"

Run PRAGMA integrity_check on the real DB and confirm it returns 'ok'. If not ok, run the WAL rebuild: sqlite3 data/jarvis_trader.db '.dump' | sqlite3 data/jarvis_trader_clean.db and replace the original.
Delete or rename engine/jarvis_trader.db (the 0-byte ghost) to engine/jarvis_trader.db.ghost so it cannot accidentally be used: mv engine/jarvis_trader.db engine/jarvis_trader.db.ghost

Run full test suite: cd engine && .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest tests/ -q --tb=short. Target: same pass count as Sprint 16 baseline (1209 passed, 0 failures). Any test that hardcodes the old path will now fail and must be updated.
Write a one-paragraph note in docs/reports/sprint17_db_path_fix.md confirming the canonical path, listing all files updated, and the integrity check result.
All Python ruff-clean. 0 test failures.
userStories.notes: Ghost DB at engine/jarvis_trader.db is 0-byte. Real DB confirmed at engine/data/jarvis_trader.db with 6 SQLite paper trades.

userStories.title: Fix NULL pnl — complete the SQLite close_trade() write path
userStories.description: As a trader, I need paper trade P&L to be correctly written to SQLite when a trade closes so that the ValidationGatesWidget, learning loop, and all P&L endpoints show accurate numbers instead of NULL.
acceptanceCriteria: Read engine/portfolio/tracker.py close_trade() function in full. Identify: (a) where exit_price is set, (b) where pnl should be computed (entry_price vs exit_price × contract multiplier × direction), (c) the exact SQL UPDATE or INSERT that writes the closed trade back to SQLite — and confirm whether pnl is included in that statement.

If pnl is missing from the UPDATE statement: add it. For futures contracts, pnl = (exit_price - entry_price) × quantity × contract_multiplier for LONG, and (entry_price - exit_price) × quantity × contract_multiplier for SHORT. MCL multiplier = 100 (micro crude oil = 100 barrels). MNQ multiplier = 2 (micro Nasdaq = $2/point). Use a INSTRUMENT_MULTIPLIERS dict in config.py if one exists, otherwise add it.

After the fix, manually close a test trade by inserting an open paper_trade row into engine/data/jarvis_trader.db, then calling close_trade() via a test script, and confirming the closed row has a non-NULL pnl value.

Run the existing paper trades in SQLite through a retroactive pnl calculation: for all 6 existing SQLite trades with NULL pnl, if entry_price and exit_price are both non-NULL, compute and UPDATE pnl in place. Write this as a one-time migration script at engine/scripts/backfill_pnl.py and run it.
Confirm the ValidationGatesWidget endpoint now returns non-NULL PF and Sharpe values: GET http://localhost:8010/paper-validation/summary/eod — response should have numeric values, not null.
Run full test suite: 0 failures. All Python ruff-clean.
Append findings to docs/reports/sprint17_db_path_fix.md: what the pnl write bug was, what the fix was, what the contract multipliers are for each instrument.
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-04-03. close_trade() now computes pnl with contract multipliers (MCL=100, MNQ=2, MES=5, MGC=10). backfill_pnl.py written at engine/scripts/backfill_pnl.py. Sprint17_db_path_fix.md updated with pnl fix details.

userStories.title: Unify dual storage — migrate 416 JSON trades into SQLite
userStories.description: As the system operator, I need all 416 paper trades currently stored in JSON files to be migrated into SQLite so that the database is the single source of truth and all endpoints, validation gates, and learning loops see the complete trade history.
acceptanceCriteria: Locate the JSON trade files: find the path(s) where paper trades are stored as JSON. Likely candidates: engine/data/paper_trades/*.json, engine/paper/*.json, or engine/data/trades.jsonl. Run: find engine/ -name '*.json' -path '*/paper*' -o -name '*.jsonl' | head -20 to identify them.

Read the JSON schema for one trade record. Map each JSON field to the corresponding SQLite paper_trades column. Note any fields that exist in JSON but not in SQLite (add columns if needed via ALTER TABLE) and any fields in SQLite that don't exist in JSON (these stay NULL).

Write a migration script at engine/scripts/migrate_json_to_sqlite.py that: (a) reads all JSON/JSONL trade records, (b) computes pnl for closed trades if not already present using the multiplier logic from US-1702, (c) INSERTs each record into paper_trades with ON CONFLICT IGNORE to avoid duplicates, (d) prints a summary: records_read, records_inserted, records_skipped_duplicate.

Run the migration script: cd engine && .venv/Scripts/python scripts/migrate_json_to_sqlite.py. Confirm output shows approximately 416 records_read and 410 new records_inserted (6 already exist from prior SQLite writes).

After migration, update the paper trade write path so all new trades write ONLY to SQLite going forward — remove or archive the JSON write path. Add a comment: '# JSON write path removed Sprint 17 US-1703 — SQLite is now canonical'.

Verify the ValidationGatesWidget now shows the correct trade count (target: close to 416 total, minus any that were still open at migration time): GET http://localhost:8010/paper-validation/summary/eod — trades_closed field should be non-trivial.

Verify the learning loop consolidator can now see all trades: cd engine && .venv/Scripts/python -c "from learning.consolidator import TradingMemoryConsolidator; import asyncio; c = TradingMemoryConsolidator(); print(asyncio.run(c.consolidate_daily()))"
Run full test suite: 0 failures. All Python ruff-clean.
Write docs/reports/sprint17_storage_unification.md documenting: JSON file location(s), record count before/after, schema mapping, any schema changes made to paper_trades table.
userStories.notes: 416 trades in JSON (source of truth), 6 in SQLite. Migration must compute pnl for any closed trades missing it.

acceptanceCriteria: Check if these files exist on disk: engine/strategies/experiment_log.py, engine/strategies/run_experiment.py, engine/strategies/search_strategy.py. Run: ls engine/strategies/ to see the full listing.

If files exist: verify they are importable (python -c 'from strategies.experiment_log import ExperimentLog; print("OK")') and git add + commit them as 'feat: recover n-autoresearch experiment loop files from prior session'.

If files do NOT exist: reconstruct from docs/session-logs/session-2026-04-03-n-autoresearch-experiment-loop.md which contains the full code from the prior Node session. Create all three files at engine/strategies/.

Verify rl_trainer.py in engine/strategies/ has WFE tracking additions from the n-autoresearch session. If missing, add: after each walk-forward fold evaluation, compute wfe = fold_pf_walkforward / fold_pf_insample and log to the experiment log.

Create engine/strategies/mes_search_space.json defining the MES parameter grid: timeframes ['15m','1h','4h'], stc_os [10,13,15,18,20,23,25], stc_ob [75,78,80,83,85,88], stop_atr_mult [0.40,0.50,0.60,0.70,0.80], t1_atr_mult [0.80,1.00,1.20,1.50,2.00], regime_required [3,4,5].
Add a CLI entry point: python -m strategies.run_experiment --symbol MES --config strategies/mes_search_space.json --n 1 should run 1 experiment and print the WFE result without error.
Add 3 unit tests in engine/tests/test_experiment_loop.py: ExperimentLog instantiation, dummy experiment log/read roundtrip, search_strategy returns valid param dict from seeded prior result.
Run full test suite: 0 failures. All Python ruff-clean.

userStories.title: MES search space — run first 10 experiments and report best WFE
userStories.description: As a trader developing MES as a future instrument, I need the first 10 walk-forward experiments run across the MES parameter search space so we have an initial WFE map and can determine whether any configuration shows promise toward the 0.50 gate.
acceptanceCriteria: Using the CLI from US-1704, run 10 experiments: python -m strategies.run_experiment --symbol MES --config strategies/mes_search_space.json --n 10. The search_strategy should select configurations intelligently (not random grid) — first 5 should be space-covering samples, next 5 should exploit the best region found in the first 5.

Each experiment must log to engine/strategies/experiment_log.json: config_used (all param values), wfe, pf_insample, pf_walkforward, sharpe_walkforward, trade_count, walkforward_window_months, timestamp.
After all 10 complete, print a summary table: rank by WFE descending, show top 3 configs with their WFE, PF_wf, and Sharpe_wf values.

Evaluate: if any config has WFE >= 0.30 (halfway to gate), note it as a promising region for Sprint 18 experiments 11-30. If no config exceeds WFE 0.15, the 1h STC signal type may have no MES edge — note that Sprint 18 should pivot to 4h timeframe experiments.
Write docs/reports/sprint17_mes_experiment_round1.md with: the 10 configs tested, their WFE results, the best config, and the recommendation for Sprint 18 experiment direction.

Add GET /experiments/mes/status to engine/routers/strategies_router.py returning: {experiments_run: int, best_wfe: float, best_config: dict, wfe_gate_passed: bool, gate_threshold: 0.50, sprint18_recommendation: str}. Read from engine/strategies/experiment_log.json.
Run full test suite: 0 failures. Dashboard build: 0 TypeScript errors. All Python ruff-clean.
userStories.notes: WFE gate for MES is 0.50. MES currently at 0.09 with default 1h/OS=15 params. 10 experiments establishes baseline map.
